static_traits.name: Lin Peiting
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk to, but has not yet told anyone about negative thoughts toward the boss
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; has not received psychotherapy in the past; no similar psychological problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good cooperation, neutral tone; able to do some self-reflection, but tending to use 'should'-style absolute standards and predictive judgments; moderately negative emotions, attention and work motivation affected by negative thinking

basic_info.main_problem: Holding persistent negative thoughts about the boss at work, believing he always errs and will never get it right, leading to decreased work drive and affected mood.
basic_info.core_demands: These negative thoughts are affecting my work performance and overall well-being, and I hope to be able to deal with and manage them effectively.

core_beliefs: Leaders must be perfect, cannot make mistakes

special_situations.event: About a month ago, the boss made a spelling error in an important email
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As a boss one should not err; the boss's mistakes embarrass me and may affect work
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to suppress these thoughts as unimportant, but they keep recurring
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will never get it right / he always makes mistakes

special_situations.event: Receiving an email from the boss
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The boss's emails likely contain errors; leaders should not err
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: When receiving email, waits for him to make a mistake to 'prove' one's own judgment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: He will surely make mistakes again this time

special_situations.event: During team meetings, communicates with the boss or observes his performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As a leader, any mistake is unacceptable, must perform perfectly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining high criticism and tension toward one's boss, work engagement declining and lacking patience with colleagues
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If he is not perfect, things will be messed up by him

core_conflict.wish: Longing for reliable, error-free leadership and a sense of order, pursuing controllability and certainty
core_conflict.fear: Worrying others' mistakes will embarrass oneself or harm work, fearing loss of control and uncertainty
defense_goal: Protecting oneself from the Anxiety of uncertainty and loss of control by maintaining strict absolute standards and a critical stance

object_relations.self_representation: Picky subordinates who are easily affected by others' mistakes
object_relations.object_representation: An incompetent leader who repeatedly errs

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When receiving an email from the boss or anticipating his mistakes in team meetings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Viewing one error as his overall incompetence, believing he will keep erring (transference: seeing him through an all-good/all-bad lens)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, inquiring tone, inviting specific facts and pro-and-con examples; avoiding judgment, helping see complexity and gray areas.

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently judging leaders with 'should/must' standards (e.g., 'as a boss cannot err')
Internalizing the external expectation that leaders should be 'perfect without error' as one's judgment criterion

positive_force: Willing to seek help and participate in CBT strategies such as reality testing
Able to acknowledge that everyone makes mistakes, and notices the boss once successfully managed a large project
Has some social support (a few friends)
negative_force: Catastrophic prediction, overgeneralization and black-and-white thinking prominent
Judging leaders with introjected 'should'-style perfection standards
Negative emotions affect work motivation and focus, and she shows irritability toward colleagues
In work situations, over-focuses on mistakes and ignores positive information

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic predictions about the boss and black-and-white negative automatic thoughts recur
antecedent: Receiving an email from the boss
Recalling a spelling mistake in an important email
target_behavior.core_reason: Generalizing one error into overall incompetence, driven by introjected perfection standards, and worrying about falling into embarrassment and loss of control again
target_behavior.function: Seeking control by presetting worst outcomes, temporarily easing Anxiety from uncertainty
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased work motivation, impaired attention, low mood, overall happiness affected

antecedent: When triggered by negative thinking at work
Interactive and pressured situations in team meetings
target_behavior.core_reason: Absolute expectations of leaders trigger frustration and tension, displacing emotions onto colleagues
target_behavior.function: Releases tension and frustration, briefly relieving inner pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal relationships affected, declining team collaboration quality
